resale_co.name: Resale Certificate (Continued Certificate of Occupancy)
resale_co.issued_by: Borough of Haworth Building Department (Construction Official)
resale_co.lead_time: About 2 to 3 weeks; two inspections are needed (fire and building)
requirements: Smoke detectors on every level (battery units allowed in existing 1 and 2 family homes); basement detector on the basement ceiling at the foot of the stairs
Carbon monoxide detectors within 10 feet of bedrooms in the hallway (not inside bedrooms)
Sump pump must discharge onto the property or street, not into the Borough sewer
Pool: compliant locking gate and fencing
House number near the front door light, 4 to 6 inches high, contrasting colors
Handrails where there are 4 or more steps
Sidewalks, curbs and gutters in safe, even condition
No fire extinguisher needed (form notes the February 3, 2025 change)

fees.label: Resale certificate application fee (single and multi-family)
fees.quote: FEE: $100 application Fee. Check payable to: Borough of Haworth.

fees.label: Re-inspection after a failed inspection
fees.quote: $25 for each re-inspection after failed inspection.

fees.label: Certificate of Continued Occupancy, residential (Borough code)

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Resale Certificate Application (Residential) with closing date, seller and buyer details and an inspection contact, and submit it with a $100 check payable to the Borough of Haworth to the Building Department, 300 Haworth Avenue (building@haworthnj.org, 201-384-8824). Both fire and building inspections are scheduled from this one application.

evidence.quote: If you are selling your home a Re Sale Certificate Residential is required.
Two inspections are required, fire and building.
February 3, 2025 Gov. Murphy states no fire extinguishers needed.

No person shall sell or lease any residential or commercial unit or building, or occupy or use any portion of a residential or commercial unit or building after such unit or building or portion thereof has been vacated or sold, or in which there has been a change in occupancy, until the owner/landlord shall first have applied for and secured a Continued Certificate of Occupancy therefor from the Construction Official of the Borough of Haworth.

resale_co.notes: Borough Code 12-11.2 (Continued Certificate of Occupancy) and the fee section 12-1.5e3 were read through the ecode360 print view. The Building Department form (revised 2/25/2025) covers both the building and fire inspections for one $100 fee. The Construction Official's email is Rsherrow@haworthnj.org. The 'Re Rental' certificate and the Landlord Identity Registration are rental items, not resale items.

requirements: Approved smoke detection and carbon monoxide detector installed per NFPA 72 and N.J.A.C. 5:70-2.3
Battery smoke and CO detectors are allowed in existing 1 and 2 family homes; electric systems must be interconnected
Smoke detectors on every level, within 10 feet of sleeping areas in a common area, not within 3 feet of an outside door, window or air vent
No fire extinguisher required (per the Borough's 2/25/2025 form)

authorities.name: Haworth Bureau of Fire Prevention (Fire Official), inspected as part of the Borough Resale Certificate
authorities.lead_time: The whole resale process takes about 2 to 3 weeks.

fees.label: Certificate of Compliance for smoke alarms (Borough code)
fees.quote: Supplementing N.J.S.A. 52:27D-192 et seq., shall be $35.

authorities.how_to_apply: Apply through the Building Department's Resale Certificate Application; the form says two inspections are required, fire and building. The Fire Protection Subcode/Fire Official (Alan Silverman) inspects Tuesday and Friday, 12:00 to 2:00 pm.

evidence.quote: Resale Certificate shall not be issued for any structure unless an approved “Automatic Fire Detection System” and
The fee for inspection or reinspection and issuance of a Certificate of Compliance by the Bureau of Fire Prevention pursuant to P.L. 1991, c.92

fire_cert.notes: In practice the smoke/CO check is one of the two inspections done under the Building Department's $100 Resale Certificate. Borough Code 14-1.9g still sets a separate $35 fee for the Bureau of Fire Prevention's smoke alarm Certificate of Compliance; it is not clear whether that is charged on top of the $100. Fire Official email firemusik@aol.com is from the NJ DCA fire directory (survey 4/2/2026); the Borough phone is 201-384-4785.

other_items.label: Sump pump discharge
other_items.detail: Sump pumps must empty onto the property or the street and cannot be connected to the Borough sewer; checked during the resale inspection.

other_items.label: Sidewalks and curbs
other_items.detail: Sidewalks, curbs and gutters in front of the home must be kept in safe, even condition; checked during the resale inspection.

open_questions: Is the $35 Bureau of Fire Prevention smoke certificate fee (Code 14-1.9g) charged in addition to the $100 Resale Certificate fee?
Is there a faster-service fee for closings less than 2 to 3 weeks out? None is published.
